en: The Meaning of the Emergence of the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones of the Vajraśekhara Yoga,

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Greatly Wise and Broad-Knowing, who was granted the honorary title of Special Advancement and Acting Minister of State Ceremonial, at the Great Xing Temple, by Imperial Decree.
I am able, O Tathāgata, Benevolent One!

Out of compassion for the delusions of the three realms and six destinies, which constantly arise from the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases (*skandha-dhātu-āyatana*), beings undergo birth and death through false attachments. They vainly calculate what is non-existent as real, like flowers in the sky, and remain ignorant of the pearl within their robes, though it exists. Thus, I withdrew my traces from the Tuṣita Heaven and descended to Central India, establishing a city of transformation to receive them and employing the removal of filth to entice them.

When the conditions for those of great lineage had matured and the time for proclaiming the three secret teachings had finally arrived, he withdrew to abide in his own *svasaṃbhogakāya*, occupied the celestial palace of Akaniṣṭha, and entered the *Amogharāja-samādhi*. There, he gathered all the sages and worthies, abolished the gradual stages of the *bhūmis*, and revealed the sudden principle of the *Samatā* and *Prativedha* [Bhūmis].

From the ocean of the Samantabhadra-vajra nature, he manifests countless加持 (adhiṣṭhāna) form bodies; thereafter, he expounds the secret mantras of the Samantabhadra-vajra vocal activity, demonstrates the secret mudrās of the Samantabhadra-vajra physical activity, and awakens the wisdom of the Samantabhadra-vajra mental activity, thereby establishing the gateway of liberation for the three vajra activities of sentient beings.

Those who do not understand believe that moving the limbs and joints is no different from mere play, and that reciting the mantras of the *vidyā-kāya* merely results in further attachment; how could they know that entering here and emerging there, employing the shallow to achieve the profound, is like Vajrapāṇi just mounting a lion and suddenly lashing out with his royal paws, so that as soon as he presses down upon a hill, it is already leveled?

This is the source and stream of the inconceivable; it is not yet within the realm of those of the three stages of worthiness or the four fruits of arhatship—how could it be something that ordinary, limited minds can grasp through mere conjecture?
Therefore, those who attain it enter right concentration through the five faculties;
they illuminate the Great Void amidst the myriad phenomena;
and they draw forth the Buddha-realm to universally purify all sentient beings.
Gathering all mental states into a single unified wisdom,
the practitioner first abides in a semblance of realization and thereby receives the power of empowerment!
Those whose defilements are thin perceive a slight radiance of the Dharma and attain a portion of samādhi!
The one who has entered deeply understands both emptiness and form as a duality; thus, there is the essence of universal purity!
When habitual tendencies and obscurations are cleared away without remainder, then the source of tranquil illumination and its functional manifestations are both fully discerned.

The Dharma King freely bestows equal benefit and profit; yet he knows that all Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment are primordially and eternally abiding, and that the assembly of Great Bodhi never fails to be in accord.
Those of external paths are obstructed by self-grasping;
those of the Two Vehicles are stalled by their realization of emptiness.
Those with superficial sentiments fail in their discernment of what to adopt and what to reject;
those of shallow intelligence are deluded by existence and non-existence. Consequently, they shatter the boat and the bridge themselves, making it impossible for them to reach the destination.
As for the mind of Samantabhadra as it is, which penetrates deeply into the wisdom of perfect luminosity—this is the great manual for practicing yoga by Bodhisattvas of the True Word (Mantra).

Thereafter, one is able to stabilize the mind of bodhi, adorn the characteristics of the mind, reveal the Dharma-treasury of the mind, accomplish the supernormal powers of the mind, and extinguish the conceptual proliferation of the mind; therein, one gives rise to clear knowledge and vision to bring sentient beings to maturity, abiding in the gate of correspondence to perform all the works of a Buddha.

Therefore, from the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom (*ādarśa-jñāna*), there arises the Vajra-Sameness Manifest Enlightenment Body; this is Akṣobhya Tathāgata in the eastern quadrant of the stupa’s center.
From the Wisdom of Equality (*samatā-jñāna*), there arises the Meaning-Equivalence Manifest Enlightenment Body; this is Ratnasambhava Tathāgata in the southern quadrant of the stupa’s center.

From the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation (*pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna*), there arises the Dharma-Equivalence Manifest Enlightenment Body; this is Amitābha Tathāgata in the western quadrant of the stupa’s center.

Through the Wisdom of Accomplishing What Is to Be Done (*kṛtyānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*), there arises the Body of Equal Enlightenment (*samabhisambodhi-kāya*) whose activity is impartial; this is the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi in the northern part of the central square of the stūpa.
Through the wisdoms of the four Tathāgatas, the four Bodhisattvas of the Pāramitās are born.

It is, indeed, the mother who gives birth, nurtures, and sustains all the sages and holy ones of the three periods of time; it thus seals the wisdom of the essential nature of the *dharmadhātu*, which is the Body of Self-Enjoyment (*svasaṃbhogakāya*), namely, Vairocana Tathāgata at the very center of the stūpa.

The four bodhisattvas of close attendance are precisely the seals of those four pāramitās; from them arises the essence of immeasurable great compassion, and from them emerges the protection of immeasurable skillful means.
From the firm essence of the enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, Vajrasattva is born!
From the essence of the four means of attraction of the enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, Vajrarāja is born!
One gives rise to Vajra-Love toward the stainless and pure essence of the awakening of all Tathāgatas!
One gives rise to Vajra-Excellent toward the essence praised by all Tathāgatas according to their respective merits!
Thus, in the eastern realm of Vajratejas-alaṃkāra, there are the four attendant bodhisattvas of Akṣobhya Tathāgata;
they are accomplished through the great precepts and the perfection of patience of all Tathāgatas.
From the meaning of the great adornment of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra-Jewel is born!
From the meaning of the great majestic radiance of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra-Sun is born!
From the meaning of the great fulfillment of the wishes of all Tathāgatas, the Vajradhvaja arises!
From the meaning of the great joy of all Tathāgatas, the Vajrahāsa arises!
He is the fourth attendant bodhisattva of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava in the southern realm of Jewel Radiance and Merit,
accomplished through the non-abiding perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) of all Tathāgatas.
From the sovereign, undefiled wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the Vajradharma is born!
From the wisdom of all Tathāgatas that has eternally severed the latent tendencies (*vāsanā*), the Vajratīkṣṇa is born!
From the wisdom of all Tathāgatas in turning the great wheel of Dharma, the Vajra Cause arises!
From the wisdom of all Tathāgatas in transcending verbal proliferation and conceptual play, the Vajra Secret Speech arises!
These are the four close-attendant bodhisattvas of the Tathāgata Amitāyus in the Western Dharma-Treasury Realm of the Great Lotus.
They are accomplished through the great wisdom-pāramitā of the samādhi of all Tathāgatas.
From the gateway of the skillful arts of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra-action is born!
From the gateway of the great compassionate armor of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra-protection is born!
From the gate of the fearless subduing of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra Fang is born!
From the gate of the sustaining accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, the Vajra Fist is born!
This is the realm of the transformative wheel of action in the north, consisting of the four attendant bodhisattvas of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi;
it is accomplished through the perfection of great diligence of all Tathāgatas in never abandoning sentient beings.

These sixteen Great Beings hold in their hands what are all the emblems of their respective samādhis; when one contemplates these objects to seek their underlying meaning, how could they be far removed?

For instance, in accordance with the realm of sentient beings entering the gates of the six pāramitās, from within the ocean of the essential nature of all Tathāgatas and the four wisdoms, there arise the Bodhisattvas of the Four Means of Integration—Vajra Hook, Lasso, Chain, and Bell!

By means of summoning, sustaining, firmly retaining, and gladdening, they receive and uphold all instructions within every site of enlightenment (*maṇḍala*). When humans and devas obtain these, they gather as a community of those seeking liberation;

when sages and worthies employ them, they reach out to the masses who are deluded and inverted. Thus, it is those who occupy their respective stations outside the four gates of the stūpa who exercise these functional applications.
It is from the wisdom initiated by the four Bodhisattvas that this arises.

These sages cannot remain at ease; though their original palaces and observatories are as vast as the sky, they hasten to cover them with the palm of their hand in order to respond to the requests of all quarters.

If a practitioner of mantra who abides [in this state] can enter this samādhi, they will be able to raise these clouds and oceans of offerings and thereby accomplish the practice of benefiting both self and others; such is the great significance of the thirty-seven deities of the central mandala.
In this way, by abiding in the *Mūrdhaja-samādhi*, he merely manifests the body of Mūrdhaja!

As for why there is a unique assembly of the Five-Wheel Kings (*pañcakula-rāja*) above the stupa, it is because all the bodies of the Mūrdhajās are subsumed within this supreme wisdom of the five mūrdhas. That which cannot be fathomed even by the directions is the *uṣṇīṣa* (cranial protuberance) of the Buddha.
This most supreme Dharma is likewise such that its limits cannot be reached; therefore, it is called the "Crown" (mūrdhan).
Furthermore, as the King of the Five Crowns is the sovereign lord who governs all mantra-honored ones, he is called the "King" (rāja).
Regarding the five crown-cakras (*makuṭa-cakra*), the Golden Cakra is the most supreme; otherwise, who would know that there is but this one uniquely transcendent Dharma?
Therefore, from the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara downward, all have gathered in fear and taken refuge.

Furthermore, below there are sixteen Vajradhara deities, manifested through the transformation of the courageous bodhicitta of all Tathāgatas. They also clarify that when the Tathāgata was practicing his path, there were dust-like mental obstructions and afflictions, which he shattered with this vajra-wisdom;
and after his great enlightenment, he perfected dust-like gateways of various types of knowledge, which he employed with this vajra-wisdom.

Therefore, he again manifested his fierce, evil, and terrifying form, wielding wisdom of great majesty to subdue those who are difficult to tame; at his roar, the trichiliocosm trembled, and with a mere glance, the hosts of demons were struck with fear and fled.
Thus, the Mother of Ghosts recoiled in terror and withdrew her tracks, while the Elephant-Headed One, fearing his power, drew far away.
Even Maheśvara, the lord of great delusions, was harmed by him and thereby attained perfect enlightenment!
Thus we know that his former reliance on wrath was, in fact, nothing other than great compassion.
These vajras are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and the drops in the dust; now, sixteen are cited here, for the meaning of "dust-like numbers" does not exceed these.

Furthermore, all other great beings and celestial beings are manifestations of bodies that appear according to the inclinations of those who behold them, serving as ladders and rafts across the mountainous peaks of error and the ocean of suffering; these, too, arise from the gateway of the skillful karmic activity of the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana.

Therefore, this Ratnastūpa may be called the comprehensive epitome of the secret intent of the One Vehicle; how much more so since the paths of both the provisional and the ultimate are fully realized herein?

As for such matters as the hundred thousand samādhis, including the Universal Manifestation of the Physical Body, the four immeasurable minds, the sequence of operations for the six pāramitās as skillful means for benefiting others, and even the practice of traveling to all Buddha-fields without rising from one’s seat to make offerings, serve, and bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings—by means of inconceivable perfuming, it subtly transforms the realm of sentient beings.

Regarding such principles and applications, while other sūtras may contain only the names and titles without their actual methods, this teaching alone is complete in its functions and ritual procedures.
Because all these belong to the Mahāyāna, their transmission and reception are difficult to accomplish.

Even if a Dharma-transmitting Ācārya, having carefully selected, finds one who is a suitable vessel, he must first bestow upon them the Bodhisattva’s natural precepts (*prakṛti-śīla*). He then leads them into the great assembly Dharma-maṇḍala, where they invoke the worthies and sages of the Vajradhātu, receive the empowerment of the nectar of the Vajrayāna, and only thereafter are shown the threshold of entry into the Buddha-mind.
Otherwise, the practitioner would gain no benefit and the transmitter would incur transgression.
Therefore, from the Buddha himself downward, they have successively entrusted one another with the charge:
"The Lion of the Śākyas received it from Vairocana Tathāgata and vowed to transmit it to Vajrasattva!"
Vajrasattva attained it and transmitted it for several hundred years to Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva;
Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva received it and transmitted it for several hundred years to Ācārya Nāgabodhi.
Furthermore, it remained for several hundred years until it was transmitted to the Acharya Vajrabodhi.

By the power of his compassionate vows, the Acharya Vajrabodhi intended to spread [the teachings] throughout the Middle Kingdom; thus, carrying his water jar and staff, he arrived at the Imperial Capital in the seventh year of the Kaiyuan era. In the fourteenth year, he suddenly found the right person and, according to his solemn pledge, transmitted them to the Acharya Amoghavajra.
"Subsequently, there have been those to whom the transmission of its branches was entrusted; if one follows the lineage of [Master] Xiang, it is merely according to this.

According to our own teaching, for anyone who receives this consecration (*abhiṣeka*), Vajrasattva will eternally abide within their body and mind, acting as a protective screen for the sovereign mind (*cittarāja*) to lead it toward the Way. Although they have not yet realized entry [into the ultimate state], they are born from the Dharma and receive the name "Vajra"; they are already counted among the ranks of Bodhisattvas. For anyone who touches or beholds them, this shall be regarded as a cause for awakening (*bodhi*).

The *Ritual for the Emergence of the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones of the Vajraśekhara Yoga* (Kongōchō yuga sanjūshichi son shusseigi), according to the Lingyun (Reiun) collated edition, states at its end:
"It was completed on the first day of the fifth month in the third year of the Jōkyō era."
Revised again on the twenty-fourth day of the same month.
The text of the practice manual contains many errors; I hope to obtain a good edition to correct them.
Jingyan, age forty-eight.
